[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended books include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. "The Devil Wears Prada" by Lauren Weisberger: Shares a behind-the-scenes look at the glamorous world of celebrities.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. "The Royal We" by Heather Cocks and Jessica Morgan: Explores complexities of female relationships and British royal romance.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. "The Interestings" by Meg Wolitzer: Follows a group of friends and explores themes of talent and ambition.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. "The Mothers" by Brit Bennett: Delves into identity, motherhood, and consequences of choices.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. "The Last Romantics" by Tara Conklin: Follows four siblings and their struggles with love and family secrets.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. "The Age of Light" by Whitney Scharer: Based on the life of Lee Miller, exploring art, identity, and sacrifices.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. "Daisy Jones and The Six" by Taylor Jenkins Reid: A fictional rock band story exploring fame and creativity.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 8. "The Immortalists" by Chloe Benjamin: Follows siblings told their death dates by a fortune teller, exploring family and choices.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 9. "The Address" by Fiona Davis: Set in the Dakota apartment building, exploring identity and community.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 10. "The Last Equation of Isaac Severy" by Nova Jacobs: Follows a woman inheriting a mysterious equation, exploring family secrets and meaning.  
[PREFERENCE] User is interested in "The Royal We" by Heather Cocks and Jessica Morgan.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "The Royal We" is described as a delightful, engaging, and thought-provoking novel combining romance, drama, and social commentary.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] **Plot Overview:** The story follows Bex Porter, an American college student who meets Prince Nicholas at Oxford and navigates the challenges of royal life.
